newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Electronics budge Taiwan stocks to 7-yr high close.
newsitem.headline: Electronics budge Taiwan stocks to 7-yr high close.

text.p: Red-hot buying on electronics and China-concept shares pushed Taiwan shares to a slightly higher close on Wednesday -- just enough to notch another seven-year high. Brokers said prices likely would firm further.

The index surged as high as 8,753.89 but faded due to late profit-taking, eking out a gain of just 34.25 points or 0.39 percent to close at 8,713.49. It was the fifth rise in as many sessions for the weighted index.
The close surpassed a seven-year closing high of 8,679.24 recorded on Tuesday. The index has not closed higher since ending at 8,922.67 on May 9, 1990.
After weeks of modest volume, market turnover surged to an extremely heavy T$207.4 billion, the highest level since the market hit an all-time high of T$238.9 billion on April 8.
Electronics, which had led recent gains, were up 4.59 percent, with chipmaker United Microelectronics up the daily seven percent limit to T$96.5 and computer giant Acer up T$5 to T$90.5.

"Buying is now focussing too much on electronics, especially semiconductor shares, as investors are buying the sector for a 1998 dream, anticipating a sound (year-ahead) outlook," said National Securities manager Allen Huang.
Some brokers are worrying over electronics' stellar rise.
"Some have started to think electronics have become over-valued and doubt whether the sector can continue to rise," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.
Chen nevertheless noted that some 10 electronics shares will go ex-bonus issue by mid-July, a strong sign that electronics should continue to attract the most buyers until then.
Almost all electronics shares that went ex-bonus issue in the past month had surged some 20-50 percent, brokers said.
Opto-electronics and power supply maker Liton was limit up to T$106 on Wednesday, its ex-bonus issue date.
